sentences.text: Placodus featured a heavy skull and a short neck, while its abdomen was protected by unique armor made of bent, right-angled ribs.
Before scientists understood its full anatomy, fossils of this animal were once mistaken for fish teeth.
The genus was first described by Agassiz in 1833, and its family, Placodontidae, was later established by Cope in 1871.
This creature specialized in a durophagous diet, crushing hard-shelled prey like bivalves, molluscs, brachiopods, and crustaceans.
Its back teeth were broad and flattened to effectively crush these tough foods.
Propulsion in water relied on flattened tails and short, likely webbed feet, while firmly connected, dove-tailed vertebrae kept the trunk rigid.
The type species is P. gigas, described by Agassiz in 1833, alongside P. inexpectatus from 2008, with 34 recorded fossil occurrences known today.
Living approximately 240 million years ago during the Middle Triassic, fossils have been found in Central Europe, China, France, Germany, and Poland.
